findings.reason: an implementation node reading §7 as written would reintroduce an already-landed field and option; the section must mark them landed so the node's scope is the JT-60SA set, not the field.
findings.text: §7 states "BenchShot therefore gains a machine field" and "The same node adds one command-line option, `scripts/spine_benchmark.py --machine`", but both already exist: `imas_ambix/spine_bench/shots.py:27` declares `machine` on BenchShot and `resolve_shotset_version` (line 74) already compares `(shot.machine, int(shot.shot_id), shot.role)`, and `scripts/spine_benchmark.py:50` already declares `--machine` (refused without `--shots` at line 34). The plan's own comments record the work as landed (`jtmm-shotset-machine`, 2026-10-05), so the §7 body is stale and describes existing machinery as proposed — the exact "rebuilds what exists" failure this review exists to catch

findings.reason: the only caller is the symbol's own test, which is removed with it, so the retirement action is unchanged; the wording should be corrected to "no production caller" but no design decision turns on it.
findings.text: §6 retires `mast_angle_to_canonical` on the stated premise that it "has no caller", but it has a caller: `tests/test_cocos.py:16` imports it and `tests/test_cocos.py:76` calls it, so the section's interface account ("ambix retires one public definition and adds none") omits that the removal also deletes its test

reuse_search-1.reason: Acted in plan v122: section 7 describes BenchShot.machine and --machine as landed on 2026-10-05 and leaves only the JT-60SA frozen set to do.

reuse_search-2.reason: Acted in plan v122: section 6 says mast_angle_to_canonical has no production caller; its only caller, its own test in tests/test_cocos.py, retires with it.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new module hides its substantial behaviour behind one entry point (`selene_deck.write_phase_description`, `eddb_remote.RemoteEddbExtractor`, `tokamap_export.export_tokamap_directory`), and the §7 EQDB extension adds a request/record type to one transport rather than spreading a second extractor.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — placement (paths.py), the pin table (`gs/artifact_resolution.py`), the identity registry (`gs/machine_identity.py`), the store engines, the convention scorer, the referee and the EDDB store each keep a single named owner that the plan extends; no forked placement or path-resolution path is introduced.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — `public_definitions` 0, `cli_options` 0, `mcp_views` 0, `refusal_families` 0; every open section that adds surface names what it retires or why nothing can be (§2 "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §5 "adds one data file and no public definition or refusal family"; §6 retires `mast_angle_to_canonical` and keeps every exported name; §7's two EQDB types, the machine field and the CLI option each carry a retirement or replacement statement).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §7 presents machinery that already exists in the tree (`BenchShot.machine`, `scripts/spine_benchmark.py --machine`, `resolve_shotset_version`'s triple compare) as work still to be added, and §6 rests a retirement on a caller claim the code contradicts.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one wrapper the plan creates (`measure_diiid_convention` over the generalised `measure_convention`) is justified in its own text by keeping existing callers unchanged; every other section extends an owner rather than layering over it.
